user.title: Connect to your Hikvision NVR
user.description: Use a device account with remote access rights. Operator is enough for live view and playback; admin is only needed for reboot.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the NVR. Check the host, the HTTP port, and that ISAPI/Hikvision-CGI is enabled.
error.invalid_auth: Wrong username or password, or the account is locked out after too many failed attempts.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log.

abort.wrong_device: Those credentials belong to a different NVR.

data_description.stream: Main stream is full resolution. Sub stream is much lighter and starts faster.
data_description.snapshot_stream: Sub stream keeps thumbnails cheap on large systems.
data_description.events: Only these become binary sensors. Untick what you do not need -- a capable NVR reports far more than most people want.

enable_notifications.name: Enable event notifications
enable_notifications.description: Tell the NVR to announce its events, not just record them. A trigger set to record only fills the disk while Home Assistant never sees the event. Existing actions are kept; this only adds Notify Surveillance Center.

device_id.description: Serial, host, or config entry id.

event_type.name: Event types
event_type.description: Limit to these event types. Defaults to all of them.

channel.name: Channels
channel.description: Limit to these channels. Defaults to all of them.

notifications_disabled.title: Detections are recorded but not reported
notifications_disabled.description:
{count} detection triggers on this NVR ({triggers}) are set to record only, with no Notify Surveillance Center linkage. The NVR will save motion clips but never tell Home Assistant, so those binary sensors stay off.

Run the **Hikvision NVR: Enable event notifications** action to add the linkage. It keeps every existing action and only adds the notification.
